mekayis.metin: (قَيَأَ) الْقَافُ وَالْيَاءُ وَالْهَمْزَةُ كَلِمَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ. قَاءَ يَقِيءُ قَيْئًا، وَاسْتَقَاءَ اسْتَفْعَلَ مِنَ الْقَيْءِ. وَيَقُولُونَ لِلثَّوْبِ الْمُشْبَعِ الصِّبْغِ: هُوَ يَقِيءُ الصِّبْغَ.

kaikki_vikisozluk.e: قَاءَ • (qāʔa) I (non-past يَقِيءُ (yaqīʔu), verbal noun قَيْء (qayʔ))
kaikki_vikisozluk.t: From the root ق ي ء (q y ʔ). The initial uvular and final glottal may point to onomatopoeia for retching, with parallel developments in other Afroasiatic languages, if not inherited from Proto-Afroasiatic, encountered in Ge'ez ቄአ (ḳeʾä), present ይቂእ (yəḳiʾ, “to vomit”), Tigre ቀኣ (ḳäʾa, “to vomit”), Hebrew קָא (qāʾ), present יָקִיא (yāqīʾ, “to vomit”), and similarly in Egyptian qꜣꜥ, qjs (“to vomit”), qꜣ, qꜣꜣ (“to be putrid; to vomit”).
